title: Observational study on quality assurance of image-guided biopsies and biopsy channel resection in soft tissue and bone sarcomas
summary: In this non-interventional observational study, data from the daily care of sarcoma patients in Tübingen will be collected and evaluated according to quality assurance criteria. The focus will be on the procedure for taking a tissue sample (biopsy), including its accuracy, colour marking and histopathological analysis. The quality and assessability of the tissue sample is crucial for subsequent treatment planning. However, biopsies of sarcomas or suspicious space-occupying lesions can be complicated by not taking enough material or by tumour cells being "seeded" in the biopsy channel. This non-interventional, observational study is designed to help improve quality standards for such biopsies. No study-related tests or therapies will be performed, and there will be no study-related risks.
conditions: Soft tissue sarcomas, bone sarcomas and gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST)

interventions.name: Systematic collection of data on biopsy, surgery and disease progression in patients scheduled for image-guided percutaneous punch biopsy of the space-occupying lesion (soft tissue or bone sarcoma or GIST) and neo-adjuvant therapy.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with suspected soft tissue sarcoma, bone sarcoma or GIST
- Indication & performance of an image-guided biopsy of the mass
- Indication for neo-adjuvant therapy regimen
- Written consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Metastatic stage of disease
- Patients incapable of giving consent or no written consent
